label: Copy phase of short sequences: fed-back token in {2,k,t,3} while outputting p/r/f/y/3/d
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.02% of steps). 98.5% of its mass is in the copy phase, mostly at recall_idx 1-3 (the 1-3 steps right after the first copy output), with heavy concentration in short sequences (L=3: 24x lift, L=4: 5.5x; together 79% of mass). The input token is almost always one of 2, k, t, 3 (86% of mass): an original token the model has already output and fed back. The token being output next is usually p, r, f, y, 3 or d (p alone is 20x lift). The strongest activations (up to 0.23) are on L=3 sequences such as "t r f <DEL> [t] r", where the fed-back first token is in {t,3,k,2} and both remaining tokens are in {p,r,f,y}. That narrow conjunction has 97% precision but covers only about 3% of activations. The feature essentially never fires in the original phase (1.4% of mass, only at orig_idx 3) or on the delimiter, and it is silent on first occurrences of tokens. The broad predicate gets about 50% recall at about 10% precision on dev; the token-set conjunctions do not explain why many matching contexts in longer sequences stay inactive, so the explanation is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=2 (+5.02), phase=2 & in_tok=k (+4.59), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+4.54), phase=2 & in_tok=3 (+4.36), phase=2 & out_tok=3 (+3.34), t=3 & prev_tok=f (+3.13). Lower it: L=4 & recall_idx=-1 (-3.54), in_first=1 (-1.71), t=6 (-0.60), next_out=- (-0.14).
